jd:
Model-based systems / simulation engineer
Junior to mid
Product company that ships 1D plant models in Modelica next to controls and test rigs. A small simulation team owns OpenModelica models so mechanical and controls engineers can share the same translational plant instead of maintaining ad-hoc MATLAB scripts. Hiring to strengthen day-to-day Modelica modeling and OpenModelica simulation on that team.

Day to day:
- Complete and review Modelica models that use Modelica Standard Library mechanical components
- Wire acausal connect equations for 1D translational plants (mass, spring, damper, force)
- Simulate in OpenModelica (omc or OMEdit) and extract steady-state and transient KPIs from the result
- Keep parameter sets and initial conditions stable so QA can rerun the same experiment
- Pair with mechanical engineers on “the diagram simulates but the numbers look wrong” issues

Required skills:
- Comfortable writing Modelica connect equations for MSL Translational components
- Can distinguish parallel vs series spring-damper topology in 1D
- Can run a model in OpenModelica (omc script or OMEdit) and read a plotted trajectory
- Understands second-order step response: steady state F/k, damping ratio, peak overshoot

Nice to have:
- Familiarity with OMEdit diagram view and result files (*_res.mat)
- Experience with Modelica.Mechanics.Translational.Sources.ConstantForce
- Prior work on test-rig, actuator, or isolation-mount plant models
- Comfort reading omc translation errors when a connect is missing

Constraints:
- Assessment focuses on completing the provided OpenModelica translational plant — not redesigning the stack or adding 3D MultiBody, FMI export, or a controls controller
- Do not test Dymola licenses, MATLAB/Simulink, or commercial Modelica libraries in this challenge
- Candidate works in a desktop environment with Terminal, OpenModelica, OMEdit, and VS Code available
- Starter files on the desktop are shared scenery; do not require inventing a different physical domain
prompt: A stubbed Modelica model of a 1D mass-spring-damper (lab test-rig translational fixture) is on your desktop. The Modelica Standard Library components are already declared. Your job is to complete the connections, simulate the plant in OpenModelica, and report steady-state position, peak position, and damping class.
